Fabiana, it's Priya. I just walked out of the year-end review, and I wanted to call you before the end of the day. That was one of the best presentations the board has seen this year. Three things stood out. You opened with the numbers, not with excuses. When the CFO pushed back on the budget, you stayed calm and reframed it. And you gave the credit to the team in Monterrey, which people noticed. The board has approved the second port for panels, so your recommendation is now policy. And one more thing: I'd like you to lead the Asia regional review next spring. It's a stretch goal, I know, but your track record says you're ready. Let's talk about it on Monday. Congratulations, and enjoy your weekend.

Hey Fabiana, it's Daniel. Congratulations on the review, everybody's talking about it. Since you're finishing your English program, here's some advice from someone who learned the hard way. When I finished my German course, I stopped practicing completely. I lost all the momentum, and six months later I could barely order a coffee in Berlin. So keep it simple. Listen to one English podcast every week. Try to speak first in at least one meeting a week. And once a month, record yourself presenting and listen back, even if you hate your voice. Oh, and if you want a practice partner before the Asia review, I'm happy to help. Just send me a message.

Fabiana looks back on the program. First, in the diagnostic, she mapped what she could already do in English. Then she learned to run vendor calls and negotiate contracts. Next, she handled the fire in Penang and persuaded Sales and Finance. After that, she managed the typhoon crisis from start to finish. Finally, she presented the whole year to the board and set her next stretch goal.
